sections.normalized_html: The amount of paint (in liters) used to cover a wall is given by the expression [MATH: \dfrac12w^2+\dfrac34,] where [MATH: w] is the width of the wall in meters. How much paint is used when the width of the wall is [MATH: \dfrac54\,\textrm{m}?]
sections.readable_text: The amount of paint (in liters) used to cover a wall is given by the expression [MATH: \dfrac12w^2+\dfrac34,] where [MATH: w] is the width of the wall in meters. How much paint is used when the width of the wall is [MATH: \dfrac54\,\textrm{m}?]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
To determine how much paint is used when the width of the wall is [MATH: \dfrac54\,\textrm{m},] we evaluate the expression at [MATH: w=\dfrac54.]

First, replacing [MATH: w] with [MATH: \dfrac54] in the expression, we obtain

[MATH: (1)/(2)w^{2} + (3)/(4)|=; (1)/(2) × w^{2} + (3)/(4)|=; (1)/(2) × ((5)/(4))^{2} + (3)/(4)|=; (1)/(2) × (25)/(16) + (3)/(4)|.]

Then, evaluating the resulting expression, we get

[MATH: (1)/(2) × (25)/(16) + (3)/(4)|=; (25)/(32) + (3)/(4)|=; (25)/(32) + (24)/(32)|=; (49)/(32)|.]

Therefore, the amount of paint used is [MATH: \dfrac{49}{32}\,\textrm{L}.]
